prerequisites: 100% presence at all laboratory training courses
Materials Science 1 (recommended, or acquire necessary prerequisite knowledge through independent study)

learning_outcomes.text: Acquaint students with materials used in mechanical engineering and with various methods of their processing.

syllabus_topics: Iron-carbon alloys and influence of other elements
Fundamentals of metallurgy (classical metallurgical processes, special metallurgical processes)
Phase transformations in ferrous alloys (austenitization, pearlitic, bainitic and martensitic transformation, tempering, T-T-T diagrams)
Heat treatment of ferrous alloys (annealing, quenching, face hardening)
Heat treatment in controlled atmospheres (carburizing, nitriding, carbonitriding, nitrocarburizing) and hot working
Classification of steels and their designation
Nonferrous metals and their alloys, processing
Powder metallurgy and applications, technical ceramics
Structure and mechanical properties of plastics
Assessment of quality of cast irons
assessment_rules: The final examination covers the content of both Materials Science 1 and Materials Science 2.
bibliography: CALLISTER, W.D.,Jr. Material Science and Engineering: An Introduction, J.Willey & sons, N.Y., 1994 (In English)
